override_flags.description: Cited as sole source across at least 10 distinct claims (PP2.1-1, PP2.1-4, PP2.1-6, PP2.2-1, PP2.2-5, PP2.2-11, PP2.3-1, PP2.3-10, PP2.4-3, PP2.3-RC3). All cost and lead-time figures citing only this domain count as single-source regardless of URL count within domain.

Vendor own-website used as sole source for capability, project, and market position claims: zbgboiler.com (VC22, VC23), en.zozen.com (VC24), coalbiomassboiler.com/taishan (VC25), vyncke.com (VC27), thermaxglobal.com (VC16, PP2.1-11), cheemaboilers.com (VC19 partial), exportersindia.com (VC19 Cethar).
APAC aggregate market sizing used without country-level breakdown for SEA context: VC3 (APAC 41% of global industrial boiler market), PP2.3-9 (APAC 12.8% biomass CAGR).
The Edge Malaysia article dated FY2019 context used for Boilermech market share figures (50-60% Malaysia, 25-30% Indonesia) — over 5 years old for a market share claim.

All UN Comtrade trade data (Indonesia HS8402 imports, India exports, China exports) accessed exclusively via trendeconomy.com aggregator rather than official comtrade.un.org. All five such claims (VC4-VC9, PP2.1-7) are single-domain and scored Low accordingly.

Wikipedia used as primary or sole citation for financial/company facts: VC18 (ISGEC revenue INR 6,245 crore), VC26 (Vyncke revenue ~EUR 200M). Wikipedia itself cites no audited source for Vyncke revenue.

PP2.4-7 cites 'bainbridge.com/sector-analysis/industrial-boiler-services-id-b7x2f9' as if it were Bain & Company. bainbridge.com is NOT bain.com. The domain appears to be an unrelated entity. This citation should be treated as unverified secondary-trade, not primary-research-firm. The BCG source in the same footnote is valid; bainbridge.com reduces to 1 credible source.

VC13 / PP2.1-8 cites volza.com export shipment count (India 49%, China 24%) marked as 'paywalled primary; cited as confirmed via web search summary' — the underlying data was never directly accessed. Scored Low.
12 claims carry explicit [ASSUMED-N] tags: ASSUMED-1 through ASSUMED-12. All scored Low per override rules.

weak_claims_for_deep_research.claim_text: Chinese OEMs price chain-grate and FBC packages 20-35% below Indian OEM equivalents
weak_claims_for_deep_research.why_weak: THE central quantified claim of the stage's primary pain point (margin compression). Both sources are Chinese boiler vendor/vendor-adjacent blogs — effectively a single source family. No independent price benchmarking from buyer surveys, trade association, customs unit-value data, or IEA/OECD energy equipment cost tracking. A vendor blog quoting competitor pricing is not evidence.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.suggested_query: Search IEA or World Bank procurement cost benchmarks for industrial biomass boilers SEA 2022-2025; OR search Thermax/ISGEC annual reports for average selling price per unit disclosed; OR search ASEAN Centre for Energy industrial energy equipment cost surveys; OR search Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) capital cost per tonne FFB for biomass boiler component

weak_claims_for_deep_research.claim_text: Palm oil mill boiler outage costs $50,000-$183,000 per day in lost production (45 t/h FFB, 20% oil extraction, CPO $850/tonne)
weak_claims_for_deep_research.why_weak: Critical financial quantification used to justify severity of both PP2.2 (warranty exposure) and PP2.4 (aftermarket downtime). Single secondary-trade source (Indonesian industry blog). The calculation is plausible but the blog presents it without sourcing the mill throughput or extraction assumptions. Used twice across the document. MPOB or GAPKI industry association data would provide a verifiable throughput and yield basis.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.suggested_query: Search MPOB (Malaysian Palm Oil Board) annual statistics for average CPO mill throughput (FFB/tonne/hour) and extraction rate 2022-2024; OR search GAPKI Indonesia palm oil statistics for processing cost and downtime impact per tonne FFB; OR search World Bank commodity price monitor for CPO reference price 2024

weak_claims_for_deep_research.claim_text: Standard tube bundle/economizer lead time 6-12 weeks from Indian OEM to SEA end-user; boiler shell 8-14 weeks; control panels 4-8 weeks
weak_claims_for_deep_research.why_weak: Core evidential claim for PP2.4 (thin aftermarket network). The specific lead-time ranges are the primary quantification of the aftermarket pain. Single vendor blog source with no corroboration from OEM annual reports, logistics benchmarks, or end-user testimony. A vendor blog quoting competitor delivery times is not independent evidence. Indian boiler industry association (IBMA) or end-user maintenance managers would provide credible primary data.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.suggested_query: Search IBMA (Indian Boiler Manufacturers Association) or Engineering Export Promotion Council India for industrial boiler export lead time and logistics data; OR search Thermax or ISGEC annual reports for aftermarket/spares revenue and delivery time KPIs disclosed; OR search Indonesia/Malaysia industrial maintenance benchmarking reports for OEM spare parts lead times in capital equipment

source_diversity_summary.notes: Primary sources total 14 of ~48 unique domains cited (29%). The remaining 71% are secondary sources. coalbiomassboiler.com alone is sole source for 10+ distinct claims. No industry association (IBMA, CIBA, MPOB, GAPKI) cited directly. No government statistics agency data (BPS Indonesia, DOSM Malaysia, NSO Thailand) cited. Trade data routed through TrendEconomy aggregator rather than UN Comtrade directly.
